'''Marilyn Meinhardt Burns''' (born April 11, 1941){{r|eb}} is a mathematics educator and the author of over a dozen children's books on mathematics.{{r|eb}}

==Career and recognition==
Burns is a 1958 graduate of the [[Wellington C. Mepham High School]] in [[North Bellmore, New York]].{{r|mepham}} After receiving a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from [[Syracuse University]] in [[Syracuse, New York]], and teaching in elementary and middle schools in Syracuse, Burns founded  Math Solutions, an educational resource provider, in 1984.{{r|hay}} Burns pursued graduate studies at Syracuse University, [[San Francisco State University]], and the [[University of California at Berkeley]].{{r|mepham}}

In 1975, the National Science Teachers Association and the Children's Book Council cited Burns's book ''The I Hate Mathematics! Book'' in "outstanding science books for children".<ref name=eb />

In 1991, the [[Bank Street College of Education]] in New York awarded Burns an honorary doctoral degree.{{r|bankstreet}}

In 1995 the Mepham High School Alumni Association listed Burns in their Hall of Fame.<ref name=mepham />

In 1996, the National Council of Supervisors of Mathematics honored Burns with the Ross Taylor/Glenn Gilbert National Leadership Award "for her influence on mathematics education".{{r|rosstaylor}}

In 1997, the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] honored Burns, "a mathematics educator with enormous scope and influence", with the [[Louise Hay Award]] for Contributions to Mathematics Education.<ref name=hay />

In 2010,  the [[Association of Educational Publishers]] inducted Burns into the Educational Publishing Hall of Fame.{{r|cblohm}}

In 2012, the [[Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation]] awarded Math Solutions a $2.2 million grant "to fund the development of a Web-based diagnostic tool that will help middle school teachers assess students' computational and problem-solving skills".{{r|gates}} The end product of this grant was Math Reasoning Inventory, an assessment tool developed by Burns in collaboration with K–12 teachers, which is available without cost to teachers and administrators.{{r|scholastic}}
